G000555.narrative: Gillibrand votes most often on economics and public finance, with her votes split between in favor and against across that area. She voted in favor of bills to fund the government, set a $35 monthly cap on insulin costs for Medicare and private insurance, and require more disclosure of campaign spending. She voted against canceling protections for endangered species and a federal budget plan for 2025. On armed forces and national security, she voted in favor far more often than against, including a bill to fund the military and set defense policies. She also voted in favor of most bills in international affairs, transportation, and science and technology.

M001231.narrative: The largest share of Mannion's votes on record fall under congressional rules and procedures, where he voted in favor more often than against. On economics and public finance bills, he voted against at a higher rate — including a no vote on a bill making appropriations for military construction and veterans programs. His votes on armed forces and energy bills fell close to evenly between in favor and against. On crime and law enforcement bills, he voted in favor more often than against, including yes votes on the Stop Child Care Scams Act of 2026 and the Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act.

S000148.narrative: Schumer votes most often on economics and public finance bills, where his record is split nearly evenly between votes in favor and against. On armed forces and national security bills, he votes in favor at a much higher rate than against. He also leans in favor on international affairs, transportation, and science and technology bills. He voted in favor of bills to fund the government, cap insulin costs under Medicare, and set defense policies. He voted against bills that would have removed federal protections for certain wildlife species and canceled rules on gender identity in food programs.

R000622.narrative: Josh Riley votes most often on congressional procedure, economics and public finance, and — tied for third — energy and national security bills. On economics and public finance, he votes against bills more often than in favor; for example, he voted against appropriations bills for agriculture programs and military construction. On energy bills, he votes in favor more often than against. On national security, he voted in favor of removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, but voted against removing forces from Lebanon.

L000606.narrative: George Latimer's votes fall most often in areas covering congressional rules and procedures, economics and public finance, and armed forces and national security. On economics and public finance votes, he voted against more often than in favor. On congressional procedural votes, he voted in favor more often than against. His votes on armed forces and national security, energy, and crime were more evenly split. He voted in favor of the ARTIST Act and a resolution to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, and voted against military construction and veterans affairs appropriations bills.

L000600.narrative: Langworthy votes most often on congressional procedure, economics, and national security matters. On energy bills, he votes against more than in favor — opposing 83 out of 143 energy votes. On international affairs, he votes in favor most of the time, supporting 72 out of 126 votes in that area. On national security bills, he also leans in favor, voting yes on 62 out of 151 votes. Notable no votes include bills to direct the removal of U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, as well as a bill on Ukraine aid.

S001201.narrative: Suozzi votes most in areas involving congressional procedure and defense, and he votes in favor more often than against in both. On economics and public finance, his votes in favor and against are more evenly split than in other areas. He voted in favor of directing the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran, and in favor of a bill to authorize support for Ukraine. He also votes in favor more often than against on government operations and international affairs bills.

G000602.narrative: Gillen votes most often on congressional procedures and rules, supporting most of these measures. On economic and finance issues, she votes against more bills than she supports. She votes in favor of most defense and security measures, as well as most crime and law enforcement bills. Her energy votes are mixed, supporting about half of energy-related measures. Her voting pattern shows different stances across policy areas, with the most activity on congressional procedures.

K000402.narrative: Kennedy votes most on congressional procedure bills, where he sides in favor more often than against. On economics and public finance bills, he votes against more often — he voted no on several appropriations measures. On armed forces and national security, his votes in favor and against are split close to evenly; he voted yes on a measure to support Ukraine and yes on removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran. On energy bills, his votes go both ways, while on crime and law enforcement bills, he votes in favor more often than against.

L000599.narrative: Lawler votes most often on bills related to congressional procedures, economics and public finance, and military and national security. On armed forces and international affairs, he votes in favor more often than against — for example, he voted yes on a bill to authorize support for Ukraine. When he takes a side on economics and public finance bills, he more often votes against than in favor. He also votes against most energy bills he has cast votes on.

N000002.narrative: Rep. Nadler votes most on congressional procedure, armed forces, and economics issues. On congressional procedure bills, he votes in favor more often than against. On armed forces and national security bills, his votes split nearly evenly between in favor and against — he voted in favor of a bill directing the president to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran, and against a similar resolution on Lebanon. On economics and public finance bills, he votes against more often than in favor, including a no vote on a bill making appropriations for military construction and veterans agencies.

T000478.narrative: Tenney votes most on congressional procedure, armed forces and national security, economics and public finance, international affairs, and government operations and politics. On armed forces and international affairs votes, she votes in favor more often than against. She voted in favor of the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2026. She voted against War Powers resolutions that would have directed the president to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran. On economics and government operations votes, her record is split between in favor and against.

G000599.narrative: Rep. Goldman votes most often on issues related to Congress, economics and public finance, and national security. On economic and public finance bills, he votes against more often than in favor. On energy bills, he votes in favor more often than against. He voted yes on the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act and the Stop Child Care Scams Act of 2026. He voted against the Cashless Bail Reporting Act.

L000598.narrative: LaLota votes most often on congressional procedures, economics, defense, energy policy, and international affairs. He votes against most bills in economics, energy, and congressional procedures, while voting in favor of most defense and international affairs bills. He voted against directing the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran under the War Powers Resolution. He voted in favor of the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act and the American Battlefield Protection Program Amendments Act.

R000579.narrative: Ryan votes most on Congress, Economics and Public Finance, and Armed Forces and National Security issues. On economics and finance bills, Ryan votes against more often than in favor. On armed forces and national security bills, Ryan also votes against more often than in favor — he voted yes on resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran, but voted no on military construction and Veterans Affairs appropriations. On energy bills, Ryan votes in favor more often than against.

T000486.narrative: Torres votes most often on Congressional matters, where he voted in favor 29 times and against 13 times. On economics and public finance, he voted against bills more often — 76 against compared to 38 in favor. His votes on armed forces and national security were split, with 65 in favor and 57 against. In international affairs, he voted in favor 42 times and against 43 times. On government operations and politics, he voted in favor 31 times and against 14 times.

M001206.narrative: Rep. Joseph D. Morelle of New York votes most on congressional procedures, national security, and economic issues. He votes against economic and public finance bills more often than in favor. His armed forces votes are nearly evenly split — he voted in favor of a bill authorizing support for Ukraine and a resolution to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, but voted against a military construction and Veterans Affairs appropriations bill. On congressional procedures and government operations, he votes in favor more often than against.

O000172.narrative: Ocasio-Cortez votes most on congressional procedure and armed forces issues, and she also votes often on economics and international affairs. On economics, she votes against more bills than she supports — she voted against the Community Bank Deposit Access Act of 2025. On armed forces, her votes go in both directions; she voted in favor of resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran, but voted against appropriations for military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs. On government operations, she votes in favor more often than against.

G000597.narrative: Garbarino votes on Congressional procedures, armed forces and national security, and government spending more than other issues. On Congressional procedures and economics and public finance, he votes against more bills than he votes in favor of. He voted against a resolution directing the removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran and against a bill to authorize support for Ukraine. On international affairs and government operations, he votes in favor more often than against. He voted yes on a veterans benefits expansion act and housing legislation.

M000317.narrative: Malliotakis votes most on congressional and procedural matters, where she leans against, and on armed forces and national security, where she voted in favor in 77 of 124 directional votes. On international affairs, she voted in favor in 68 of 89 directional votes; she voted against measures to direct the removal of U.S. armed forces from Lebanon and Iran under the War Powers Resolution. Her votes on economics and public finance are split, with support for housing and veterans bills alongside opposition to the Stop Child Care Scams Act.

M001244.narrative: Senator Moody votes most often on economics and public finance, where she sides in favor the large majority of the time. On international affairs, she votes in favor more often than against, but voted against resolutions that would have directed the removal of U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran. On environmental protection, she voted to repeal EPA rules setting air pollution limits for rubber tire factories and vehicle emission standards for California, and her votes in this area go against environmental protection measures nearly every time. She also voted in favor of defense funding and rules for stablecoin companies.

F000484.narrative: Fine votes most often on Congress issues, economics, and military matters. On Congress-related bills, he votes neutral on most measures but votes against more non-neutral bills than he supports. He votes in favor of most military and defense bills, like declaring Iran a terrorism sponsor and requiring agencies to exclude China from financial groups if China threatens Taiwan. On economic issues, he leans toward voting in favor, supporting bills like expanding federal housing programs and canceling DC's tax law to keep federal tax cuts.

F000476.narrative: Rep. Maxwell Frost votes most often on congressional rules and procedures, economics and public finance, and armed forces and national security, with energy a near-equal fourth area. On economics and public finance bills, he votes against more often than he votes in favor. He votes against more armed forces and national security bills than he votes in favor of. On energy, he votes in favor of most bills that come to the floor. He voted in favor of resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran, and voted against appropriations bills for military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs.

D000628.narrative: Rep. Neal P. Dunn votes most often on congressional procedures, where he votes against bills more than in favor of them. On armed forces and national security, he votes in favor more often than against — he voted yes on a veterans benefits expansion act and no on resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran. On international affairs, he votes in favor far more often than against. On economics and public finance, his votes are split between in favor and against.

S001217.narrative: Scott votes most often on economics and finance issues, with roughly equal votes in favor and against different spending and financial measures. He regularly supports military funding and policies, and votes in favor of most international affairs measures. Scott often votes against science and technology initiatives. He has voted to cancel several environmental protections and government regulations while supporting some government funding measures and military policies.

F000472.narrative: Scott Franklin votes most often on congressional procedure and national security matters. He votes against most bills that fall under congressional procedure, while voting in favor of most bills related to armed forces and national security. On international affairs, he voted in favor of most bills that came before him. He voted against War Powers resolutions that would have directed the removal of U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, and voted in favor of bills expanding veterans benefits.

M001217.narrative: Rep. Moskowitz votes most often on congressional procedure, economic bills, and military matters, and on procedure votes he voted in favor more than against. On economic and spending bills, he voted against more bills than he voted in favor — for example, he voted against an appropriations bill for military construction and veterans affairs. On armed forces and national security issues, he also voted against more bills than he supported, though he voted in favor of a resolution to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran. On international affairs, his votes split about evenly between in favor and against. He voted in favor of more energy bills than he voted against.

M001216.narrative: Mills votes most often on congressional rules, economics and public finance, armed forces and national security, energy, and international affairs. He votes in favor of economics and public finance bills more often than against, while voting against more congressional procedure bills than in favor. On armed forces and national security, he votes in favor most of the time — including a yes vote on the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act. He votes in favor of most international affairs bills, but against most energy bills.

P000622.narrative: Patronis votes most on Congress-related issues, where he leans against the measures that come to a vote. He also votes often on economics and defense matters, voting in favor on most economics and defense bills. On environmental protection, he votes against most measures, while his energy votes lean slightly in favor.

H001099.narrative: Haridopolos votes most often on congressional procedure and economic issues, where he votes against more bills than he supports. On Armed Forces and National Security, he votes in favor at a higher rate than against. His record on Energy bills is split evenly between yes and no votes. Specific votes against include resolutions on U.S. military involvement in Lebanon and Iran, while votes in favor include a veterans benefits bill and a housing act.

M001199.narrative: Congressional procedure makes up the largest share of Mast's votes, and he votes against procedural measures more often than in favor of them. On policy matters, he votes most often on armed forces, economics, and international affairs — and leans in favor in all three areas. He voted against resolutions that would have directed the president to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran under the War Powers Resolution, and against a measure to authorize support for Ukraine. He voted in favor of a bill expanding veterans' benefits and a measure related to the American Battlefield Protection Program.

G000593.narrative: Gimenez votes most often on congressional procedure, defense and national security, and economics. On defense and national security bills, he voted in favor more often than against. On economics, government spending, and congressional procedure, he voted against more often than in favor. He voted against resolutions that would have directed the removal of U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran. He voted in favor of the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act and the Community Bank Deposit Access Act of 2025.

L000597.narrative: Rep. Lee votes most on congressional procedures, economics and public finance, military and national security, energy, and international relations. She voted against most congressional procedure bills and against most energy bills. She voted in favor of most military and national security bills and most international affairs bills. Her economics votes went both ways, with slightly more yes votes than no votes. She voted yes on the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act and voted no on resolutions to remove U.S. armed forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran.

R000609.narrative: Rutherford votes most on congressional procedure, armed forces, and economics bills. On defense and military matters, he votes in favor more often than against, and he voted against resolutions that would have directed the President to remove U.S. troops from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran. On international affairs, he votes in favor at a much higher rate than against. On congressional procedure votes, he votes against more often than in favor. He voted in favor of bills on veterans' benefits and local banking.

L000596.narrative: Luna votes most often on Congress operations, where she voted against most procedural measures. On economics and military matters, she voted in favor of most bills, including appropriations for military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs. On energy policy, she voted against most bills, including the Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Reauthorization Act of 2025. On international affairs, she voted in favor of most bills overall, though she voted against directing the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from Lebanon and Iran.

B001314.narrative: Aaron Bean of Florida votes most often on congressional procedure, economic matters, defense, energy, and international affairs. He votes in favor of most bills on economics, defense, and international affairs. On energy bills, he votes against most of them, and he also votes against most congressional procedure bills. He voted yes on the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act and several banking access bills. He voted no on resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran.

F000462.narrative: Lois Frankel votes most often on bills about Congress, defense and national security, and economics and public finance. On bills about economics and public finance, she votes against more often than in favor. Her votes on defense and national security bills are closely divided, with a slight lean toward support. On bills about Congress and government operations, she votes in favor more often than against. She voted in favor of a bill to authorize support for Ukraine and a resolution to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, and voted against an appropriations bill for military construction and veterans affairs.

W000797.narrative: Wasserman Schultz votes most often on congressional procedures and armed forces and national security issues. On procedural votes and government operations, she leans in favor. On economics and public finance bills, she votes against more often than in favor. On defense and national security votes, her record is split close to evenly, with slightly more votes against than in favor. She voted in favor of directing the president to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran, and voted against making appropriations for military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs.

D000600.narrative: Diaz-Balart votes most often on congressional process matters, armed forces and national security, and economics and public finance. On congressional process votes, he voted against more bills than he voted in favor of. On armed forces and national security bills, as well as international affairs bills, he voted in favor more often than against. On economics and public finance bills, his votes did not lean in either direction. He voted against resolutions that would have directed the president to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, and he voted in favor of the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2026.

C001127.narrative: Cherfilus-McCormick votes most often on Congress procedures, energy policy, and government spending issues. She votes in favor of most energy measures, including bills that secure energy supply chains and require energy efficiency standards for appliances. She votes against most government spending bills, including major funding measures for defense, health, education, and housing programs. She also votes against most military and international affairs bills, such as defense funding and measures involving military action limits.

P000145.narrative: Sen. Alex Padilla votes most often on economics and public finance bills, where he voted against 63 measures and in favor of 51. On international affairs, armed forces, transportation, and science and technology bills, he voted in favor more often than against. He voted yes on bills to fund the federal government, cap insulin costs for Medicare patients, and require more disclosure of campaign spending. He voted no on bills to cancel environmental protections for certain animals and to cancel rules on financial data collection.

P000197.narrative: Pelosi votes most on Congress, economics, and defense issues. On economic bills, she votes against more often than in favor. On defense and national security bills, she also votes against more often than in favor. On energy bills, she votes in favor more than against — including yes votes on the ARTIST Act and the Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Reauthorization Act. Her votes on international affairs are split, and she voted in favor of directing the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.

S001150.narrative: Schiff voted most often on economics and public finance bills, voting against measures in that area more often than in favor. On environmental protection bills, he voted in favor every time, and voted against bills that would have canceled EPA rules on air pollution from rubber tire factories and California truck pollution limits. On finance bills, he voted in favor of resolutions blocking rollbacks of consumer financial protection rules on overdraft fees and medical debt collection. His votes on transportation leaned against, while international affairs votes were split, though he voted in favor of resolutions directing the removal of U.S. forces from hostilities against Iran not authorized by Congress.

C001059.narrative: Costa votes most often on issues related to Congress, armed forces and national security, and the economy. On economic and finance bills, he votes against more than in favor. On government operations and politics, he votes in favor more than against. His votes on armed forces and international affairs are split — he voted in favor of removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran but voted against a similar measure regarding Lebanon. He also voted against military construction and Veterans Affairs spending bills.

W000187.narrative: Waters votes most on congressional procedure and rules, where she leans in favor. On armed forces and national security, her votes go both ways — she voted in favor of War Powers resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, but voted against bills for military construction and VA funding. On economics and public finance, she votes against more often than in favor. On government operations and politics, she leans in favor.

M001225.narrative: Rep. Kevin Mullin of California votes most often on how Congress operates, economics, and defense matters. On economic and defense bills, he votes against more than in favor — including a vote against a military construction and veterans affairs spending bill. On energy bills, he votes in favor more than against. On international and defense issues, he voted in favor of a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran.

C001123.narrative: Cisneros votes most often on issues related to Congress itself, and he votes in favor of most of these measures. On economic and public finance issues, which make up his second-largest category of votes, he votes against most proposals. He votes in favor of most energy-related bills but shows mixed voting patterns on defense and security matters. He tends to vote against crime and law enforcement measures.

W000830.narrative: Whitesides votes most often on congressional procedure, and in that area, he has voted in favor more than against. On economics and public finance, his votes lean against, including a no vote on military construction and veterans affairs appropriations. His votes on armed forces and national security and on energy are split between in favor and against. On crime and law enforcement, he voted in favor more often than against. He voted yes on the Stop Child Care Scams Act and on a resolution directing the removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran.

F000483.narrative: Friedman votes most often on Congress-related matters and usually votes in favor of these bills. On economics and public finance issues, she votes against most legislation. She votes in favor of most energy-related bills, including those that fund energy efficiency programs, but votes against bills that would block energy efficiency rules. On defense and military matters, she more often votes against legislation than in favor.

F000480.narrative: Fong votes most on congressional procedures and economics — and in both areas, he votes against more bills than he votes in favor. On armed forces and national security bills, the pattern flips: he votes in favor more often than against. The same is true for international affairs, where he votes in favor of most bills. His votes on energy bills are more evenly split between in favor and against. He voted against resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, and voted in favor of a veterans benefits act and a housing bill.

K000397.narrative: Kim Young votes most often on congressional procedure, defense and national security, and economics and public finance issues. On defense and national security bills, Kim voted in favor more than against — voting yes on the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2026. On economics and public finance bills, Kim voted against more than in favor — voting no on the Stop Child Care Scams Act of 2026. On international affairs, Kim voted in favor more than against. On congressional procedure votes, Kim voted against more than in favor.

G000598.narrative: Garcia votes most often on Congressional procedure matters, but takes few yea or nay positions there. He votes yea or nay most often on Energy and Economics and Public Finance bills. On energy bills, he voted in favor 86 out of 113 times. On economics bills, he voted against 74 out of 94 times. He voted in favor of resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, and voted against a bill for military construction and Department of Veterans Affairs spending.

O000019.narrative: Obernolte has cast 2,514 votes in Congress, with his most votes falling in five areas: congressional procedure, armed forces and national security, economics, international affairs, and government operations. On congressional procedure and economic bills, he voted against more measures than he voted for. On armed forces and national security, he voted in favor more often than against, including votes against bills that would have directed the president to remove U.S. troops from Lebanon and Iran. On international affairs, he also voted in favor of most measures that came before him, while his votes on government operations were split roughly even.

K000400.narrative: Kamlager-Dove votes most often on congressional procedure, economics and public finance, armed forces and national security, energy, and international affairs. On economic and defense bills, she votes against most of them — she voted against a veterans benefits expansion act and against several appropriations-related measures. On energy bills, she votes in favor most of the time. Her votes on international affairs are split — she voted in favor of War Powers resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, and in favor of a procedural measure bringing to the floor a bill to authorize support for Ukraine.

P000613.narrative: Panetta votes most often on bills related to congressional procedures, armed forces and national security, and economics and public finance. On congressional process votes and government operations bills, he votes in favor more than against. His votes on armed forces and national security are split nearly evenly between in favor and against — he voted in favor of a War Powers Resolution to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, but against a similar resolution on Lebanon. On economics and public finance, he votes against more often than in favor, including voting against military construction and veterans affairs appropriations bills.

L000582.narrative: Rep. Ted Lieu of California votes most often on congressional rules and procedures, and he is in favor of most of those measures. On armed forces and national security bills, his record is split — he voted in favor of directing the president to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran under the War Powers Resolution, but voted against military construction and veterans spending bills. He votes against most economic and public finance legislation. His votes on international affairs are mixed, including a vote in favor of a bill to authorize support for Ukraine. He is in favor of most government operations and politics measures.

H001090.narrative: Rep. Josh Harder votes most often on Congressional procedures and Armed Forces and National Security matters. On Congressional procedures, he votes in favor more often than against. On economics and public finance, he votes against more bills than he supports, including a no vote on military construction and Veterans Affairs appropriations. On Armed Forces and National Security, he votes in favor slightly more than against, including a yes vote to direct the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran. On international affairs, his votes lean slightly in favor, such as supporting consideration of a bill to authorize aid for Ukraine.

J000305.narrative: Sara Jacobs votes most often on issues related to congressional procedure, national defense, and government spending. On Economics and Public Finance votes, she voted against most bills she considered — including a bill that would have changed how states spend funds under the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program. Her record on Armed Forces and National Security is split, with votes in favor of resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, and against certain defense spending bills. She voted in favor of most Government Operations and Politics bills she considered.

A000371.narrative: Aguilar votes most often on congressional procedure, armed forces, and economics bills. On economics and public finance, he votes against more often than in favor, including a no vote on military construction and veterans affairs spending. His armed forces votes are split evenly between yes and no — he voted in favor of removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran but against removing forces from Lebanon. International affairs votes are also roughly even, with support for Ukraine authorization among his yes votes. On congressional procedure and government operations bills, he votes in favor more often than against.

C001098.narrative: Cruz casts most of his votes on economics and public finance, and more often votes in favor of those measures than against them. He has voted in favor of federal budget plans and government funding bills, while voting against some spending measures, including a bill to fund the government through December 2021. In international affairs, Cruz has voted in favor of most measures, including a resolution expressing Senate support for Israel against Hamas. He also voted in favor of armed forces and national security measures more often than against them, including a bill funding the military and setting defense policies for the year starting October 2025. His votes on transportation and science and technology bills are more evenly split.

C001056.narrative: Senator Cornyn votes across many policy areas in the Senate, and the five areas shown here are part of a larger record. On economics and public finance — where he casts the most votes — he votes in favor most of the time, including on bills to fund the federal government and a bill that set a $35 monthly cap on insulin costs for people on both Medicare and private insurance. He also votes in favor on most bills related to international affairs, national security, and science and technology. On election and voting rules, he voted against bills that would expand voter registration access and require more disclosure of campaign spending. On transportation, his votes lean in favor, though he voted against a bill to fund the FAA and airports through 2028.

C001120.narrative: Rep. Dan Crenshaw votes most often on congressional procedure, armed forces and national security, and economic policy. On Armed Forces and National Security bills, he has voted in favor more than against. On International Affairs, he has also voted in favor more than against. He voted against bills directing the president to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran. He voted in favor of the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act.

J000310.narrative: Representative Julie Johnson of Texas votes most often on bills related to congressional procedure, and she votes in favor on those bills more often than she votes against. On economics and public finance bills, she votes against more often than in favor — including a vote against a bill to fund military construction and the Department of Veterans Affairs. On armed forces and national security bills, she also votes against more often than in favor, including voting against a measure to direct the President to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon. On energy bills, she votes in favor more often than against.

M001245.narrative: Rep. Menefee votes most often on issues related to Congress, agriculture and food, energy, environmental protection, and international affairs. In his congressional and energy votes, he leaned in favor of the bills that came to the floor. In agriculture and environmental protection, he cast no votes for or against the substance of any bill — all votes recorded in those areas were procedural. On international affairs, he voted both ways, including voting in favor of resolutions directing the removal of U.S. armed forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran.

S001224.narrative: Rep. Keith Self of Texas votes most often on congressional procedural matters, where he votes against more often than in favor. On substantive policy issues, he casts the most votes on economics, military affairs, and energy. He votes in favor of economic and military bills more often than against, while he votes against energy bills more often than in favor. On international affairs, he votes in favor more often than against. He voted against bills to remove U.S. troops from Lebanon and Iran under the War Powers Resolution, and voted in favor of bills related to community banking and veterans' benefits.

M001224.narrative: Moran votes most on congressional procedures, followed by economic and finance bills, military and national security measures, energy policy, and international affairs. On economic and finance issues, he has voted in favor more often than against, including yes votes on the American Access to Banking Act and the Keeping Deposits Local Act. He has voted in favor of most armed forces and national security bills and most international affairs measures, but voted against bills directing the removal of U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran. On energy, he has voted against most bills in that area, and on congressional procedure votes, he has voted against more often than in favor.

G000601.narrative: Goldman votes most often on congressional procedural matters, where he leans against.
